title: the DSG proficiency descriptions

banner.title: The DSG PROFICIENCY DESCRIPTIONS, R527: printed p. 58 (pdf 59) - the fourteen brief introductions: the animal trainer (little equipment beyond harnesses and leashes, but a great deal of outdoor room, with shelter and food if boarding), the armorer (a small forge, several hammers, at least one small anvil and metal files, with good ventilation and exhaust for the especially hot fire the high-quality armor irons demand), the blacksmith (the armorer's equipment in greater assortment and size, but a cruder grade of iron needing lower-quality tools), the boatwright (a major investment in tools or facilities at a carefully chosen location - boats launchable, so near water, excepting kayaks, canoes and small rowboats; the space the boat size plus 10 feet in all directions; the tools all carpentry plus pitch or tar), the bowyer/fletcher (little beyond knives and vises), the carpenter (hammers, spikes, axes, and chisels), the gem cutter (finely tooled chisels, hammers and vises, good light, sturdy safes or strongboxes), the leatherworker (punches, needles, knives, scissors, and treating oils), the miner (varying with the operation - a shallow pan and container for stream panning, but picks, shovels, shoring timbers, hammers, spikes and mining carts for a tunnel, the need growing with the tunnel), the potter (a small operation whose largest object, the kiln, limits the size of the wares), the smelter (a large, sophisticated, expensive setup: the efficient high-temperature furnace at the center, an individually operated bellows, and the iron-buckets-on-rails or cauldron/stone-trough feeding system), the stonemason (going where the work is, stone availability the limit, usually with access to a sturdy wagon and oxen), the weaponsmith (a small blacksmith's shop plus the fine finishing tools for edges and ornamentation), and the weaver (a very small area, the tabled space needed only for spinning, the initial costs a spinning wheel and loom)

consts.name: dnepBoatwrightMarginFt
consts.comment: the space a boatwright needs is roughly the size of the boat being built, plus 10 feet in all directions.

bools.name: dnepIntroFrame
bools.comment: the descriptions provide brief introductions to the various proficiencies - interested players are encouraged to learn more by reading of these arts during medieval times.

bools.name: dnepAnimalTrainerLittle
bools.comment: the animal trainer needs little specialized equipment - at most a few harnesses or leashes - though most animal training requires a great deal of room, generally outdoor space, with shelter and food also required if raising or boarding animals.

bools.name: dnepArmorerForge
bools.comment: the armorer requires a small forge, several hammers, at least one small anvil, and a collection of metal files - and since the high-quality iron and steel of most armor need an especially hot fire, good ventilation and exhaust must be provided.

bools.name: dnepBlacksmithSameButMore
bools.comment: the blacksmith's craft requires much the same equipment as the armorer's but in a greater assortment and much greater size - though working a cruder grade of iron, his tools need not be of such high quality.

bools.name: dnepBoatwrightLocationCare
bools.comment: the boatwright must make a major investment in tools or facilities and choose the location with care - excepting kayaks, canoes and small rowboats, boats must be built close enough to water for easy launching; the tools are all carpentry tools plus pitch or tar.

bools.name: dnepBowyerLittle
bools.comment: the bowyer/fletcher is another profession requiring little in the way of tools beyond an assortment of knives and vises.

bools.name: dnepCarpenterTools
bools.comment: the carpenter needs an assortment of woodworking tools including hammers, spikes, axes, and chisels.

bools.name: dnepGemCutterTools
bools.comment: the gem cutter needs a collection of finely tooled chisels, hammers, and vises, with good light sources important and most keeping sturdy safes or strongboxes to protect their valuable materials.

bools.name: dnepLeatherworkerTools
bools.comment: the leatherworker's tools include punches, needles, knives, scissors, and oils for treating the leather.

bools.name: dnepMinerVaries
bools.comment: the miner's equipment varies considerably with the type and size of the operation - panning for gold needs little more than a shallow pan and a container, while a tunnel mine involves picks and shovels to excavate, timbers, hammers and spikes to shore, and a few mining carts on a long tunnel, the need growing with the tunnel.

bools.name: dnepPotterKiln
bools.comment: the potter's operation can be quite small, the largest object being the kiln - and the kiln's size limits the size of the objects the potter can make.

bools.name: dnepSmelterFurnace
bools.comment: the smelter must set up a large, sophisticated, rather expensive operation: an efficient furnace for extremely high temperatures at the center, a bellows system usually operated by an individual to fan the fire, and a feeding system - iron buckets sliding along a rail or track through the furnace, or a huge cauldron or stone trough.

bools.name: dnepStonemasonGoesToWork
bools.comment: like a carpenter, the stonemason usually goes where there is work - the most limiting factor is the availability of stone, often gathered in the immediate area, and the mason usually maintains or has access to a sturdy wagon and a few oxen for transport.

bools.name: dnepWeaponsmithShop
bools.comment: the weaponsmith needs to maintain a small blacksmith's shop, with an additional array of tools for finishing the fine detail work of putting edges and ornamentation on weapons.

bools.name: dnepWeaverSmall
bools.comment: the weaver can work in a very small area - if the wool or cotton must be spun by the weaver, the tabled area is needed; the initial costs include a spinning wheel and loom.

examples.expr: m['dnepBoatwrightMarginFt']() != 10 or m['dnepArmorerForge']() != 1 or m['dnepSmelterFurnace']() != 1 or m['dnepMinerVaries']() != 1
examples.note: the load-bearing catch-up cells: the boatwright 10-ft margin, the armorer forge-and-ventilation setup, the smelter furnace/bellows/feeding system, and the miner pan-vs-tunnel equipment.

examples.expr: m['dnepIntroFrame']() != 1 or m['dnepBlacksmithSameButMore']() != 1 or m['dnepBoatwrightLocationCare']() != 1 or m['dnepWeaverSmall']() != 1 or m['dnepPotterKiln']() != 1 or m['dnepStonemasonGoesToWork']() != 1
examples.note: the rest of the fourteen paragraphs: the intro frame, the blacksmith, the boatwright location care, the weaver, the potter and the stonemason.
